key_insight: For financial time series forecasting, QNN performance depends more on circuit design choices—especially gate type, arrangement, and entanglement structure—than on simply increasing parameter count.
engineering_relevance: The study gives practical design guidance for building more accurate and hardware-resilient QNNs, while also showing where near-term quantum devices still face noise-related deployment limits.
method: Grid-searched 1,368 QNN configurations across encodings, ansatzes, qubit counts, depths, and cost functions.
Evaluated each model on GBP/USD forecasting using prediction accuracy, computational cost, and convergence behaviour.
Tested selected configurations on real quantum hardware (IQM Emerald) to assess noise sensitivity.
evidence_signal: The benchmark reports a best QNN achieving R² = 0.985, outperforming a classical BiLSTM baseline, while also characterizing hardware noise effects on real-device runs.
watch_item: Results are promising but practical deployment remains constrained by gate errors, decoherence, and sensitivity to circuit depth on current quantum hardware.
paper_title: Large-Scale Benchmarking of Quantum Neural Network Configurations for Financial Time Series Forecasting
